Uniqueness of Weak Solutions to One-Dimensional Doubly Degenerate Cross-Diffusion System Note: The authors acknowledge support from the National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC), grant 12471206.

Xiuqing Chen Email: chenxiuqing@mail.sysu.edu.cn Address: School of Mathematics(Zhuhai), Sun Yat-sen University, Zhuhai 519082, Guangdong Province, China Corresponding author: Corresponding author.    Bang Du Email: dubang@mail2.sysu.edu.cn Address: School of Mathematics(Zhuhai), Sun Yat-sen University, Zhuhai 519082, Guangdong Province, China
August 24, 2026
Abstract

The uniqueness of global weak solutions to one-dimensional doubly degenerate cross-diffusion system is shown. The equations model the evolution of feeding bacterial populations in a malnourished environment. The key idea of the proof is applying anti-derivative of the sum of weak solutions to the system.

Keywords: 
Nutrient taxis systems , doubly degenerate cross-diffusion , uniqueness
2020 MSC
35K55, 35K67, 35A02, 35Q92, 92C17.

1 Introduction

The aim of this paper is to study the uniqueness of global weak solutions to the initial/boundary-value problem

{ut=(u​v​ux)x−(u2​v​vx)x+u​v,x∈Ω,t>0,vt=vx​x−u​v,x∈Ω,t>0,uvux−u2vvx|∂Ω=0,vx|∂Ω=0,t>0,u|t=0=u0,v|t=0=v0,x∈Ω,\left\{\begin{aligned} &u_{t}=(uvu_{x})_{x}-(u^{2}vv_{x})_{x}+uv,\;\;&x\in\Omega,\;t>0,\\ &v_{t}=v_{xx}-uv,\;\;&x\in\Omega,\;t>0,\\ &uvu_{x}-u^{2}vv_{x}|_{\partial\Omega}=0,\,v_{x}|_{\partial\Omega}=0,&t>0,\\ &u|_{t=0}=u^{0},\,v|_{t=0}=v^{0},&x\in\Omega,\\ \end{aligned}\right. (1)

where Ω⊂ℝ\Omega\subset{\mathbb{R}} is a bounded open interval, which describes the evolution of food-consuming bacterial populations in nutrient-poor environments. The equations have been proposed to describe the dynamics in collections of Bacillus subtilis ([1], [3]). It has been shown by Winkler [2] that (1) with assumption

{ u0∈Cϑ​(Ω¯) for some ϑ∈(0,1), with u0≥0 and ∫Ωln⁡u0​𝑑x>−∞,  v0∈W1,∞​(Ω) satisfies v0>0 in Ω¯ \left\{\begin{aligned} &\mbox{~$u^{0}\in C^{\vartheta}(\overline{\Omega})$ for some $\vartheta\in(0,1)$,~with~$u^{0}\geq 0$ and~$\int_{\Omega}\ln u^{0}dx>-\infty$, }\\ &\mbox{~$v^{0}\in W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)$ satisfies $v^{0}>0$ in~$\overline{\Omega}$ }\end{aligned}\right. (2)

admits a global weak solution (u,v)(u,v) in the sense that for any φ∈C0∞​([0,∞)×Ω¯)\varphi\in C_{0}^{\infty}([0,\infty)\times\overline{\Omega}),

−∫0∞∫Ωuφtdxdt−∫Ωu0φ(⋅,0)dx\displaystyle-\int_{0}^{\infty}\int_{\Omega}u\varphi_{t}dxdt-\int_{\Omega}u^{0}\varphi(\cdot,0)dx (3)
=−∫0∞∫Ωuvuxφxdxdt+∫0∞∫Ωu2vvxφxdxdt+∫0∞∫Ωuvφdxdt,\displaystyle\qquad\qquad=-\int_{0}^{\infty}\int_{\Omega}uvu_{x}\varphi_{x}dxdt+\int_{0}^{\infty}\int_{\Omega}u^{2}vv_{x}\varphi_{x}dxdt+\int_{0}^{\infty}\int_{\Omega}uv\varphi dxdt,
−∫0∞∫Ωvφtdxdt−∫Ωv0φ(⋅,0)dx=−∫0∞∫Ωvxφxdxdt−∫0∞∫Ωuvφdxdt,\displaystyle-\int_{0}^{\infty}\int_{\Omega}v\varphi_{t}dxdt-\int_{\Omega}v^{0}\varphi(\cdot,0)dx=-\int_{0}^{\infty}\int_{\Omega}v_{x}\varphi_{x}dxdt-\int_{0}^{\infty}\int_{\Omega}uv\varphi dxdt, (4)

which satisfies

{0≤u∈C0([0,∞)×Ω¯)∩L∞((0,∞)×Ω),ux∈L2l​o​c([0,∞)×Ω¯),v∈C0([0,∞)×Ω¯)∩C1,2((0,∞)×Ω¯)∩L∞((0,∞)×Ω),vx∈L∞((0,∞)×Ω),for any fixed​T,v≥c⁡(T)>0.\left\{\begin{aligned} &0\leq u\in C^{0}([0,\infty)\times\overline{\Omega})\cap L^{\infty}((0,\infty)\times\Omega),~u_{x}\in L^{2}_{loc}([0,\infty)\times\overline{\Omega}),~\\ &v\in C^{0}([0,\infty)\times\overline{\Omega})\cap C^{1,2}((0,\infty)\times\overline{\Omega})\cap L^{\infty}((0,\infty)\times\Omega),~v_{x}\in L^{\infty}((0,\infty)\times\Omega),~\\ &\mbox{for any fixed}~T,~v\geq c(T)>0.\end{aligned}\right. (5)

The two-dimensional case was treated by Zhang and Li [4].

Our main result reads as follows.

Theorem 1.

Let (u,v)(u,v) be a weak solution to (1)-(2) satisfying (3)-(5). If 1/u0∈L1​(Ω)1/u^{0}\in L^{1}(\Omega), then (u,v)(u,v) is unique.

Without loss of generality, we suppose that Ω=(0,1)\Omega=(0,1). The key idea of the proof is the use of w⁡(t,x)=∫0x(u⁡(t,y)+v⁡(t,y))​𝑑yw(t,x)=\int_{0}^{x}(u(t,y)+v(t,y))dy, such that the uniqueness of (u,v)(u,v) is equivalent to that of (w,v)(w,v). More precisely, it follows from the L1​(Ω)L^{1}(\Omega)-conservation of u+vu+v that w⁡(t,0)≡0w(t,0)\equiv 0 and w⁡(t,1)≡‖u0+v0‖L1​(Ω)w(t,1)\equiv\|u^{0}+v^{0}\|_{L^{1}(\Omega)} which imply that (w1−w2)|∂Ω=0(w_{1}-w_{2})|_{\partial\Omega}=0 in Lemma 4. The boundedness of 1/u1/u in L∞​(0,∞,L1​(Ω))L^{\infty}(0,\infty;L^{1}(\Omega))(Lemma 2) is used to control the term v12​(v1−v2)2u1+u2\frac{v_{1}^{2}(v_{1}-v_{2})^{2}}{u_{1}+u_{2}} in (18) of Lemma 5. We obtain Lemma 5 from Lemmas 2-4 and hence the uniqueness of (w,v)(w,v) by Gronwall’s inequality.
